blockers.problem: The Case org-wide default has no artefact that can carry it. outputs[] declares settings/Sharing.settings-meta.xml and acceptance_tests[3] asserts the OWD is read from it, but skills/admin/sharing-and-visibility/references/metadata-examples.md:11 states that sharingModel and externalSharingModel 'live on the CustomObject file, not in a separate settings file', and check_sharing_model.py reads object OWDs only from *.object-meta.xml. 'sharingModel' appears zero times in plan.json, so no step sets it. Reproduced: the step test and the M2 milestone test both print '(0 object OWD(s) resolved)' and exit 0 whatever the OWD is; with <sharingModel> on Case.object-meta.xml the same command resolves it and exits 1 on ReadWrite. D5, the M2 milestone goal 'a Tier 1 agent cannot open a Billing case' and the fit-gap row 'Finance queries worked only by Finance' all rest on Private.
blockers.fix: Declare <sharingModel>Private</sharingModel> and <externalSharingModel>Private</externalSharingModel> on objects/Case/Case.object-meta.xml (M1-S01's output), add M1-S01 to M2-S05's depends_on, and reword M2-S05 acceptance_tests[3] to read the OWD from the object file. M2-S05 keeps the sharing rule and the visibility note.

warnings.problem: Both tests' descriptions state that check_validation_rules.py 'returns 1 on ANY finding including REVIEW' (the round's S1 sweep finding). It does not. emit_result() at check_validation_rules.py:102-119 returns 1 only on CRITICAL/HIGH, or on any finding under --strict, and its own docstring says why: 'MEDIUM/LOW/REVIEW are advisory and exit 0 so a build that produced correct rules with natural formulas stays green'. Neither command declares --strict. Reproduced: the guarded rules exit 0 ('Scanned 2 validation rule(s) across 2 file(s); 0 finding(s) detected'), and the unguarded ISPICKVAL(...,'') form prints the two REVIEW 'picklist logic has no explicit blank guard' findings and also exits 0. The ISBLANK constraint is carried by M3-S01's manual test [3], not by either exit code.
warnings.fix: Add --strict to both commands (verified: guarded exits 0, unguarded exits 1), or reword both descriptions to say the blank guard is carried by the manual test.

warnings.problem: acceptance_tests[0] runs check_case_management_setup.py --manifest-dir artefacts at build scope. Its assignment-rule discovery reads only <manifest-dir>/assignmentRules and does not recurse (find_xml_files, check_case_management_setup.py:62-67), while the absence guard that would skip the section does recurse (any(manifest_dir.rglob('assignmentRules'))). At artefacts/ in this layout the two disagree the moment any step writes an assignmentRules/ directory. Reproduced: with M3-S04 absent the command exits 0 ('No case management setup issues found.'); with M3-S04's correct, active rule present the identical command exits 1 on a false 'assignmentRules directory is present but contains no case assignment rule'. The step note anticipates the first state, so the first pass through the loop is green; a re-test or resume after M3-S04 is built fails on a correct build. This is a second bug in the same checker, alongside the <active>-element bug M3's milestone test [4] already records.
warnings.fix: Record the order dependence in the test description, or deepen admin/case-management-setup so find_xml_files recurses the way its own absence guard does.

warnings.problem: acceptance_tests[3], [4] and [5] each require the proof sandbox — [4] and [5] name 'M5-S02's proof sandbox' explicitly — while M5-S02 is blocked ('borrowed agent requires team_size, concurrent_workstreams, release_cadence, data_sensitivity') and ships nothing in this phase. The v3 blockers B04 and B06 were closed by moving those two ticks here, which un-deadlocked M2 and M3 as intended, but their new home names an artefact this plan does not produce. The M5 gate is still mechanically approvable (section 3 accepts a step that is blocked with a reason), so this is a tick a human is asked to make against a precondition the plan says will not exist, not a deadlock.
warnings.fix: Reword [4] and [5] to name the sandbox the release owner stands up rather than M5-S02's plan, and state in [3] that the proof plan document is outstanding while M5-S02 is blocked.

warnings.problem: D4's branch_quote is presented as one quoted block but is a splice: the Q13 heading line and the Omni-Channel branch row, with the intervening Assignment Rules branch elided and no ellipsis. Each fragment is verbatim in standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md and the branch it names is real, so the decision is grounded; the quote as written is not a contiguous string in the tree. Unchanged since v1, and the v3 verification reported all nine quotes as matching verbatim, which was a fragment-wise check.
warnings.fix: Quote the two fragments separately, or include the elided row.

warnings.problem: The planner's W08 disposition records the check_uat_case.py --file / --manifest-dir divergence as NOT FIXED because agents/ was outside its mutation scope. It is no longer divergent: agents/build-doc-keeper/AGENT.md Step 10 now instructs the --manifest-dir form and names the plan's agreement explicitly. The Process Observation asking a human to change build-doc-keeper is stale.
warnings.fix: Drop the W08 Process Observation on the next re-plan; the plan and the agent already agree.

warnings.problem: history[] holds two entries, versions 1 and 3, while the build has been through three rejections (verification envelopes at plan_version 1, 2 and 3). The v2 plan body was never archived, and the entry labelled version 3 carries a verification block whose plan_version is 2 — set-verification archives the current body before writing the new block, so an archived body carries the previous round's verdict. Not a defect in this plan's content; recorded so a reader of history[] does not read it as the full record.
warnings.fix: None for this plan. A build_plan.py change would be needed to archive on every rejection and to stamp the archived body with the verdict that rejected it.
